**SECTION D: COMPOSITION.** Write a composition of about 250-300 words on any one of the following topics.

**Topic 1.** Abortion: causes and drawbacks.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
La rédaction anglaise du BAC sanctionne autant le respect du format imposé (essai factuel et équilibré, article persuasif de magazine scolaire, récit narratif à la première personne) que le contenu. Un essai sur les causes et inconvénients d'un phénomène de société doit rester factuel, informatif et nuancé, sans jugement moral appuyé, en présentant plusieurs causes puis plusieurs inconvénients distincts ; un article persuasif pour un magazine scolaire présente une proposition claire soutenue par des arguments concrets ; un récit sur un sujet aussi grave que le mal-être d'un proche doit rester centré sur l'écoute, le soutien et l'orientation vers de l'aide, sans jamais détailler de méthode ni dramatiser inutilement la détresse elle-même. Comme le sujet propose un choix, un seul texte doit être rédigé le jour de l'examen ; les modèles ci-dessous illustrent chacun l'un des formats possibles.

## Topic 1 - Factual essay: causes and drawbacks (modèle, environ 260 mots)

Abortion remains one of the most debated topics in many societies, and understanding both its causes and its drawbacks helps explain why the debate remains so difficult to resolve.

Several factors commonly lead women to consider abortion. An unplanned pregnancy, particularly among very young women or students still pursuing their education, is one of the most frequent causes, since a baby can disrupt schooling and future opportunities. Financial hardship also plays a major role, as some families feel unable to support another child. In some cases, medical reasons are involved, when a pregnancy poses a serious risk to the mother's health or life. Finally, pregnancies resulting from rape or incest are sometimes cited as a cause, since carrying such a pregnancy to term can cause severe psychological distress.

However, abortion also carries significant drawbacks that cannot be ignored. Medically, especially when performed in unsafe or unregulated conditions, it can lead to serious complications, infections, or even death, a real danger in countries where legal access to safe procedures remains limited. Psychologically, some women experience lasting feelings of grief, guilt or regret afterwards, even when they felt the decision was necessary at the time. Abortion also remains legally restricted or entirely prohibited in many countries, including Cameroon except in specific circumstances, which pushes some women towards clandestine and more dangerous procedures. Finally, the topic often creates deep tension within families, couples and communities, given the strong religious and moral convictions many people hold on the matter.

Because abortion touches on health, law, religion and personal circumstances all at once, no single explanation can capture why it remains such a sensitive and consequential issue in societies like ours.

**SECTION D: COMPOSITION.** Write a composition of about 250-300 words on any one of the following topics.

**Topic 2.** Write a persuasive article for your school magazine in which you suggest changes in the education system of your country. Your school magazine is Students' Voice and your name is Ngongui Jose. Your address is P.O. Box 200, Ndelele.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 2 - Persuasive school magazine article (modèle, environ 260 mots)

**It's Time to Rethink How We Learn**

By Ngongui Jose, P.O. Box 200, Ndelele

Our education system has produced generations of hardworking graduates, yet I believe it is time we honestly examined what it still gets wrong, and what we could do better.

First, our curriculum remains heavily focused on memorisation and theory, often at the expense of practical, hands-on skills. A student can pass an entire science programme without ever conducting a real experiment, which leaves many of us unprepared for further study or for the job market once we graduate. I propose that schools invest more seriously in laboratories, workshops and practical sessions, even if this means reducing the sheer volume of theoretical content covered.

Second, our system places enormous pressure on a small number of final examinations, with little space for continuous assessment that reflects a student's effort throughout the year. A single difficult day can undo months of genuine hard work. Introducing more continuous assessment, properly weighted alongside final exams, would give a fairer and more complete picture of what a student has actually learned.

Third, subjects like financial literacy, civic education and mental health awareness remain almost entirely absent from our timetable, despite being essential to navigating adult life successfully. I believe these should be introduced as core subjects, not occasional talks squeezed into an already packed schedule.

None of these changes would be easy to implement, and I do not pretend to have all the answers. But if we, as students, do not raise these questions ourselves, I fear the same gaps will simply be passed on to the students who come after us.

**SECTION D: COMPOSITION.** Write a composition of about 250-300 words on any one of the following topics.

**Topic 3.** A friend of yours is about to commit suicide. You try to dissuade him or her. Tell the story.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 3 - Narrative composition (modèle, environ 270 mots)

I noticed something was wrong with my friend Achu weeks before he actually told me anything. He had stopped joining us at football practice, barely answered his phone, and when he did speak, his voice sounded distant, as if he were already somewhere else.

One evening, I decided to visit him instead of waiting for him to come to me. He opened the door reluctantly, and when I asked how he was doing, something in his face finally broke. He told me he felt like a burden to everyone around him, that his family would be better off without him, and that he had been thinking about ending his life.

I remember forcing myself to stay calm, even though my chest felt tight with fear. I did not argue with him or tell him he was wrong to feel that way. Instead, I simply asked him to tell me more, and I listened, really listened, without interrupting or rushing to fix everything at once.

When he finished, I told him honestly how much his friendship meant to me, and how devastated I would be to lose him. I asked him to promise me one thing: that before doing anything, he would come with me to speak to his older sister, whom I knew he trusted, and to the school counsellor the next morning.

He hesitated for a long time, but eventually he agreed. I stayed with him that night rather than leaving him alone, and the next day, we kept that promise together.

Achu is doing much better today. He still has difficult days, but he has support around him now, and he knows he does not have to face them alone. I am simply grateful I listened closely enough, that evening, to notice he needed someone to.

Topic 3 aborde le thème du mal-être psychologique et des idées suicidaires chez un proche : le modèle proposé se concentre volontairement sur l'écoute, le soutien et l'orientation vers une aide adaptée (famille, conseiller scolaire), sans détailler aucune méthode, conformément à un traitement responsable de ce sujet même dans un cadre scolaire fictif.
